# Setting Up a Teaching Lab {#sec-app-e}

This appendix is for instructors and lab managers who want to run the course, or a course like it. It describes what a room needs so that every team can build, solder, program and test its kit safely. Quantities assume a section of about 30 students working in teams of two or three, with up to 10 people soldering at once.

## The room

| Need | Recommendation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Layout** | A dedicated soldering bench along one wall; separate tables for pair work with laptops; an instrument shelf; lockable storage; a visible safety station | Keeps hot irons away from laptops, paper and foot traffic |
| **Power** | Hard-wired or properly rated outlets at each bench; no daisy-chained power strips; cords routed off the floor | Every station draws power at once, and crossing cords are a trip and burn hazard |
| **Ventilation** | A fume extractor at each soldering station, and confirmation from your environmental health and safety office that room ventilation is adequate | Rosin flux fumes are a respiratory irritant |
| **Surfaces** | Heat-resistant, wipeable bench tops or silicone mats at the soldering bench | Solder spatter and dropped irons |
| **Seating** | Fixed, wipeable stools at the soldering bench | Fabric chairs on casters collect spatter, build static, and roll over cords |
| **Lighting** | Task lighting at the soldering bench | Small pads and fine pitch need good light |
| **Network** | A 2.4 GHz WPA2-Personal network able to handle about 30 devices, or a dedicated travel router | Enterprise and captive-portal networks block small devices (@sec-app-b) |
| **Safety station** | First-aid kit including burn dressings, fire extinguisher, eyewash if required, posted soldering procedure and emergency contacts | Required by most institutions; makes the rules visible |

: Room requirements. {#tbl-room}

## Shared equipment (per 10 soldering stations)

| Qty | Item | Notes (Fall 2026 choice) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Temperature-controlled soldering stations with stands | 60 W, with spare tips, helping hands and a solder sucker (YIHUA 926 III) |
| 10 | Fume extractors | One per station |
| 10 | Silicone work mats | Heat-resistant, ≈ 34 × 23 cm |
| 30+ | Safety glasses | One per person soldering, plus spares |
| 2 | Spools of lead-free solder, 0.8 mm, rosin core | SAC305 |
| 5 | Flux pens | No-clean |
| 10 | Desoldering braid | One spool per station |
| 6 | Sets of 22 AWG solid-core wire, six colors | For the cut-and-strip activity and flat breadboard wiring |
| 12 | Automatic wire strippers | Covering 22 AWG |
| 15 | Flush cutters | One per station plus spares |
| 5 | Digital multimeters | With continuity beeper |
| 12 | USB-C inline power meters | For measuring board current; most cannot resolve deep-sleep currents |
| 1 | Travel router | A private 2.4 GHz network for demos |
| 2 | Burn first-aid kits | Supplementing the room's general kit |
| 1 | Small-parts organizer | Spare LEDs, resistors, buttons and headers |

: Shared equipment. {#tbl-lab-equipment}

In Fall 2026 this shared equipment cost about **$1,900** for 10 stations, and kit parts for 36 new kits about **$2,000**.

## Before the first lab

- **Kits**: count, label and test every kit; flash a kit-check sketch; pre-solder or pre-provision anything students should not do themselves (for example, locking secure elements).
- **Network**: test that 30 boards can join the room network and reach your broker or server at the same time.
- **Safety briefing**: present the soldering procedure, show the safety station and require safety glasses.
- **Staffing**: plan at least one teaching assistant per 10 students during soldering.
- **Kit policy**: decide whether kits are returned at the end of the term or can be bought, and how damaged parts are replaced.

## Running costs

Budget each term for consumables (solder, flux, wire, resistors and LEDs), replacement parts (an ESP32 or a sensor per few kits is typical), and spare tips for the soldering stations.
